lessons.summary: Eat, praise the cooking and turn down a third plate politely.

content.title: Sunday lunch at Lola's
content.scenario: Eat, praise the cooking and turn down a third plate politely.

rounds.situation: You walk into your partner's grandmother's kitchen for Sunday lunch. The whole table is covered in dishes.
rounds.tagalog: Ang bango po dito, Lola! Ano pong niluto ninyo?
rounds.translation: It smells so good, Lola! What did you cook?

chunks.note: Ang + adjective is an exclamation: 'how fragrant!'
Keep this chunk together in the middle of the sentence.
Po takes the linker -ng before a verb: 'ano pong'. Ninyo is the respectful 'you'.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Compliment the smell and ask her what she cooked, respectfully.

rounds.situation: You take the first bite of her kare-kare. Lola watches you, waiting for your verdict.
rounds.tagalog: Grabe, ang sarap po ng kare-kare ninyo!
rounds.translation: Wow, your kare-kare is delicious!

chunks.note: Grabe is an all-purpose 'wow' for anything extreme.
Sarap is the go-to compliment for food. Ang makes it an exclamation.
Ng marks whose delicious thing it is: 'the deliciousness of your kare-kare'.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Tell her the dish is delicious.

rounds.situation: Lola spoons more rice towards your plate and insists you keep eating.
rounds.tagalog: Sige po, pero konting kanin lang.
rounds.translation: Okay, but just a little rice.

chunks.note: Sige is 'okay, go ahead'. Add po for an elder.
Konting is konti + the linker -ng.
Lang means 'just, only' and softens the request.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Accept, but ask for only a small amount.

responseExercise.promptTagalog: Sige po, pero konting kanin lang.
responseExercise.promptTranslation: Okay, but just a little rice.

options.englishTranslation: Oh no, I'm completely full, Lola.
Okay, but just a little rice.
Just wrap some up for me, so I have food for tomorrow.

rounds.situation: She is already reaching for the serving spoon a third time.
rounds.tagalog: Naku, busog na busog na po ako, Lola.
rounds.translation: Oh no, I'm completely full, Lola.

chunks.note: Naku softens a refusal with a little drama.
Repeating an adjective with na intensifies it: 'very, very full'.
Short words go first: na, then po, then ako.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Turn down the third serving politely.

rounds.situation: Lola looks disappointed that so much food is left. Offer her a way out.
rounds.tagalog: Pabalot na lang po ako, para may baon ako bukas.
rounds.translation: Just wrap some up for me, so I have food for tomorrow.

chunks.note: Pa- turns a verb into a request: pabalot is 'have it wrapped'. Na lang means 'instead'.

chunks.english: so I have food to bring
chunks.note: Baon is food you take with you.
Use this ending to complete the spoken thought naturally.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Ask her to pack some leftovers so you can eat them tomorrow.

responseExercise.promptTranslation: Just wrap some up for me, so I have food for tomorrow.

lessons.summary: Catch up with an old friend using the small words locals love.

content.title: Sound natural with little words
content.scenario: Catch up with an old friend using the small words locals love.

rounds.situation: You bump into your old friend Bea at a coffee shop in Makati. You only recognise her at the last second.
rounds.tagalog: Uy, ikaw pala! Ang tagal na nating hindi nagkita.
rounds.translation: Hey, it's you! We haven't seen each other in so long.

chunks.note: Start the thought with this reusable chunk.
Pala marks a sudden realisation: 'so it's you!'
Ang + adjective again: 'how long it's been'.
Natin takes -g as a linker: 'natin' becomes 'nating'.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Show your surprise at seeing her and say it's been ages.

rounds.situation: Bea asks how you've been lately.
rounds.tagalog: Okay naman ako, medyo busy lang sa trabaho.
rounds.translation: I'm okay. Just a bit busy with work.

chunks.note: Naman softens your answer: 'I'm okay, all things considered'.
Lang downplays it: 'only a bit'.
Use this ending to complete the spoken thought naturally.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Say you're fine, only a little busy at work.

rounds.situation: You arrived twenty minutes late. Explain why.
rounds.tagalog: Na-late ako kanina kasi grabe ang traffic sa EDSA.
rounds.translation: I was late earlier because the traffic on EDSA was terrible.

chunks.note: Na- + English verb means it happened to you.
Kasi means 'because'. It's how people give reasons in conversation.
Use this ending to complete the spoken thought naturally.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Say you were late and give the reason: the traffic.

responseExercise.promptTagalog: Na-late ako kanina kasi grabe ang traffic sa EDSA.
responseExercise.promptTranslation: I was late earlier because the traffic on EDSA was terrible.

options.englishTranslation: Apparently Carlo is getting married in December!
I was late earlier because the traffic on EDSA was terrible.
How about you, how's your love life?

rounds.situation: You heard some gossip about your old classmate Carlo. Pass it on.
rounds.tagalog: Ikakasal na raw si Carlo sa Disyembre!
rounds.translation: Apparently Carlo is getting married in December!

chunks.note: Raw means 'they say'. Use raw after a vowel and daw after a consonant.
Si marks a person's name.
Use this ending to complete the spoken thought naturally.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Share the news you heard from someone else.

rounds.situation: You've talked about yourself enough. Turn the question back to Bea.
rounds.tagalog: Ikaw naman, kumusta na ang love life mo?
rounds.translation: How about you, how's your love life?

chunks.note: Ikaw naman means 'your turn': naman shifts the focus to the other person.
Keep this chunk together in the middle of the sentence.
Use this ending to complete the spoken thought naturally.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Turn the conversation to her and ask about her love life.

responseExercise.promptTranslation: How about you, how's your love life?

lessons.summary: Say what you did, what you're doing and what you will do.

content.title: Weekend stories
content.scenario: Say what you did, what you're doing and what you will do.

rounds.situation: It's Saturday evening and you're on a video call with your partner Mark's sister, Joy. She asks about your day.
rounds.tagalog: Kaninang umaga, naglaba ako at naglinis ng bahay.
rounds.translation: This morning I did the laundry and cleaned the house.

chunks.note: Kanina means 'earlier today'.
Completed aspect: mag- becomes nag-. Maglaba, naglaba.
Same pattern: maglinis, naglinis.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Tell her the chores you finished this morning.

rounds.situation: Joy asks what you did after that.
rounds.tagalog: Pagkatapos, kumain kami ni Mark sa labas.
rounds.translation: After that, Mark and I ate out.

chunks.note: Start the thought with this reusable chunk.
Completed aspect of -um- verbs: kain becomes kumain. Kami means 'we, not you'.
Kami ni Mark means 'Mark and I'.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Say you and Mark went out to eat.

rounds.situation: Joy hears a movie playing in the background.
rounds.tagalog: Ngayon, nanonood kami ng pelikula sa bahay.
rounds.translation: Right now we're watching a movie at home.

chunks.note: Start the thought with this reusable chunk.
Ongoing aspect: repeat the first syllable of the root. Nood becomes nanonood.
Use this ending to complete the spoken thought naturally.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Tell her what you two are doing at the moment.

responseExercise.promptTagalog: Ngayon, nanonood kami ng pelikula sa bahay.
responseExercise.promptTranslation: Right now we're watching a movie at home.

options.englishTranslation: Tomorrow we're going to Tagaytay to eat bulalo.
Right now we're watching a movie at home.
Are you coming with us? We're leaving around seven.

rounds.situation: Joy asks if you have plans for tomorrow.
rounds.tagalog: Bukas, pupunta kami sa Tagaytay para kumain ng bulalo.
rounds.translation: Tomorrow we're going to Tagaytay to eat bulalo.

chunks.note: Start the thought with this reusable chunk.
Contemplated aspect: repeat the first syllable, no -um-. Punta becomes pupunta.
After para, use the plain infinitive.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Tell her your plan for tomorrow and why.

rounds.situation: There's a free seat in the car. Invite Joy along.
rounds.tagalog: Sasama ka ba sa amin? Aalis kami mga alas-siyete.
rounds.translation: Are you coming with us? We're leaving around seven.

chunks.note: Contemplated aspect of sumama: sasama. Ba turns it into a question.
Keep this chunk together in the middle of the sentence.
Alis becomes aalis: a vowel root just doubles its vowel.
Mga before a time means 'around'.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Invite her and say what time you're leaving.

lessons.summary: Ask for a date, set the time and place, then book the tickets.

content.title: Ask someone out to the movies
content.scenario: Ask for a date, set the time and place, then book the tickets.

rounds.situation: You've been chatting with Mika after your dance class for weeks. You finally work up the nerve.
rounds.tagalog: Libre ka ba sa Sabado ng gabi?
rounds.translation: Are you free on Saturday night?

chunks.note: Libre means both 'free of plans' and 'my treat'.
Use this ending to complete the spoken thought naturally.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Ask if she's free on Saturday night.

rounds.situation: She smiles and says she is. Make your invitation.
rounds.tagalog: Gusto mo bang manood ng sine kasama ko?
rounds.translation: Would you like to watch a movie with me?

chunks.note: Ba takes the linker -ng before the next verb: 'bang manood'.
Sine is the everyday word for the cinema.
Use this ending to complete the spoken thought naturally.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Invite her to see a movie with you.

rounds.situation: She says yes. Suggest a place and a time to meet.
rounds.tagalog: Kita tayo sa Megamall mga alas-sais, okay lang ba?
rounds.translation: Let's meet at Megamall around six, is that okay?

chunks.note: Kita tayo is the casual short form of magkita tayo.
Keep this chunk together in the middle of the sentence.
Clock times use Spanish numbers: alas-sais.
Use this ending to complete the spoken thought naturally.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Suggest meeting at the mall at about six and check it works for her.

responseExercise.promptTagalog: Kita tayo sa Megamall mga alas-sais, okay lang ba?

rounds.situation: Saturday night at the cinema counter. The young cashier is waiting.
rounds.tagalog: Dalawang ticket po para sa alas-siyete y medya.
rounds.translation: Two tickets for the seven-thirty show, please.

chunks.note: Numbers link to the noun with -ng: dalawa becomes dalawang.
Y medya means 'and a half'.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Ask the cashier for two tickets to the half past seven screening.

rounds.situation: The cashier turns the screen to show you the seating map.
rounds.tagalog: Pwede po bang magkatabi kami, sa bandang gitna?
rounds.translation: Can we sit together, somewhere in the middle?

chunks.note: Pwede po bang opens any polite request.
Magka- means 'together': magkatabi is 'next to each other'.
Banda means 'around, near'.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Ask for two seats next to each other near the middle.

lessons.summary: Book the boat, deal with a tricycle driver and check in.

content.title: Island trip to Puerto Galera
content.scenario: Book the boat, deal with a tricycle driver and check in.

rounds.situation: You're at the ticket booth at Batangas port. The ferry office has a long queue behind you.
rounds.tagalog: Isang round trip po papuntang Puerto Galera, yung alas-diyes.
rounds.translation: One round trip to Puerto Galera, the ten o'clock one, please.

chunks.note: Start the thought with this reusable chunk.
Papunta means 'heading to'.
Yung points to a specific one: 'the one at ten'.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Ask for a return ticket on the ten o'clock boat.

rounds.situation: You'll be coming back tomorrow and want to plan ahead.
rounds.tagalog: Anong oras po ang huling biyahe pabalik bukas?
rounds.translation: What time is the last trip back tomorrow?

chunks.note: Anong is ano + -ng: 'what time'.
Huli + -ng: 'huling' means 'last'.
Pabalik means 'heading back'.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Ask the clerk when the last boat back leaves tomorrow.

rounds.situation: The boat docks. Tricycle drivers crowd the pier. You wave one over.
rounds.tagalog: Kuya, magkano po hanggang White Beach?
rounds.translation: How much to White Beach, sir?

chunks.note: Kuya ('big brother') is how you address any man a bit older: drivers, guards, vendors.
Keep this chunk together in the middle of the sentence.
Hanggang means 'up to, as far as'.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Ask the driver the fare to the beach.

responseExercise.promptTagalog: Kuya, magkano po hanggang White Beach?
responseExercise.promptTranslation: How much to White Beach, sir?

rounds.translation: That's too expensive. Can we make it fifty instead?

chunks.note: Naman here adds a gentle complaint: 'that's a bit much'.
Keep this chunk together in the middle of the sentence.
Prices often use Spanish numbers: singkwenta is fifty. Na lang means 'instead'.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Say it's too pricey and offer fifty pesos.

rounds.translation: Hi, I have a booking under the name Alex Smith.

chunks.note: Even an English 'hi' gets po for staff and strangers.
May means 'there is, have'.
Use this ending to complete the spoken thought naturally.

lessons.summary: Describe your symptoms and leave with the right medicine.

content.title: At the doctor and the pharmacy
content.scenario: Describe your symptoms and leave with the right medicine.

rounds.situation: You're sitting across from the doctor at a clinic in Quezon City. She asks what's wrong.
rounds.tagalog: Dok, tatlong araw na po akong may lagnat.
rounds.translation: Doc, I've had a fever for three days.

chunks.note: Dok is how everyone addresses a doctor.
Na after a length of time means 'already, so far'.
Ako takes the linker -ng before may: 'akong may lagnat'.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Tell the doctor how long you've had a fever.

rounds.situation: The doctor asks if you have any other symptoms.
rounds.tagalog: Masakit din po ang lalamunan ko, at inuubo ako.
rounds.translation: My throat hurts too, and I've been coughing.

chunks.note: Din follows a consonant (masakit); rin would follow a vowel.
Keep this chunk together in the middle of the sentence.
Inuubo is 'being hit by a cough': the illness is the doer.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Describe your sore throat and your cough.

rounds.situation: Before writing the prescription, she asks if you're allergic to anything.
rounds.tagalog: Wala po akong allergy sa kahit anong gamot.
rounds.translation: I'm not allergic to any medicine.

chunks.note: Wala + -ng means 'have no'.
Kahit ano means 'any at all'.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Tell her you have no medicine allergies.

responseExercise.promptTagalog: Wala po akong allergy sa kahit anong gamot.
responseExercise.promptTranslation: I'm not allergic to any medicine.

options.englishTranslation: Miss, here's my prescription from the doctor.
I'm not allergic to any medicine.
How many times a day should I take this?

rounds.situation: At the pharmacy counter, you hand the prescription to the pharmacist, a young woman.
rounds.tagalog: Ate, heto po ang reseta ko galing sa doktor.
rounds.translation: Miss, here's my prescription from the doctor.

chunks.note: Ate ('big sister') is a warm way to address a woman serving you.
Heto means 'here it is'.
Galing sa means 'coming from'.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Hand over the prescription and say where it's from.

rounds.situation: She puts the tablets on the counter. You want to be sure how to take them.
rounds.tagalog: Ilang beses ko po ba ito iinumin sa isang araw?
rounds.translation: How many times a day should I take this?

chunks.note: Ilan + -g: 'ilang beses' means 'how many times'.
Short words line up: ko, then po, then ba. Iinumin is the future of inumin.
Use this ending to complete the spoken thought naturally.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Ask how many times a day to take the medicine.

lessons.summary: View a unit, ask the right questions and agree on the rent.

content.title: Renting a condo
content.scenario: View a unit, ask the right questions and agree on the rent.

rounds.situation: The landlady, Mrs. Reyes, is showing you a one-bedroom unit in Mandaluyong. You like the view.
rounds.tagalog: Magkano po ang upa kada buwan?
rounds.translation: How much is the rent per month?

chunks.note: Start the thought with this reusable chunk.
Upa is rent. Many people also just say 'rent'.
Kada means 'every, per'.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Ask her the monthly rent.

rounds.situation: She tells you the price. Check what it covers.
rounds.tagalog: Kasama na po ba ang tubig at kuryente sa upa?
rounds.translation: Are water and electricity already included in the rent?

chunks.note: Kasama means 'included, together with'.
Keep this chunk together in the middle of the sentence.
Use this ending to complete the spoken thought naturally.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Ask whether utilities are part of the rent.

rounds.situation: She mentions an upfront payment. Ask the details.
rounds.tagalog: Ilang buwan po ang advance at deposit na kailangan?
rounds.translation: How many months of advance and deposit do you need?

chunks.note: Start the thought with this reusable chunk.
Landlords use the English terms.
Na here is a linker joining the noun to its description.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Ask how many months you have to pay upfront.

responseExercise.promptTagalog: Ilang buwan po ang advance at deposit na kailangan?
responseExercise.promptTranslation: How many months of advance and deposit do you need?

options.englishTranslation: If I sign for a year, could you lower it a little?

rounds.situation: The rent is a bit above your budget. Try to negotiate.

rounds.translation: If I sign for a year, could you lower it a little?

chunks.note: Kung means 'if'. Pipirma is the future of pumirma.
Keep this chunk together in the middle of the sentence.
Keep this chunk together in the middle of the sentence.
Nang (not ng) introduces how something is done: 'by a little'.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Offer a one-year contract in exchange for a lower rent.

rounds.situation: She agrees to a small discount. You're ready to decide.
rounds.tagalog: Sige po, kukunin ko na. Kailan po ako pwedeng lumipat?
rounds.translation: Okay, I'll take it. When can I move in?

chunks.note: Start the thought with this reusable chunk.
Kukunin is the future of kunin. Na: 'now, settled'.
Keep this chunk together in the middle of the sentence.
Pwede + -ng links to the verb: 'pwedeng lumipat'.

lessons.summary: Chat with a coworker the way Manila offices really talk.

content.title: Office small talk in Taglish
content.scenario: Chat with a coworker the way Manila offices really talk.

rounds.situation: Monday morning in the office pantry in BGC. Your coworker Paolo is making coffee.
rounds.tagalog: Uy, good morning! Kumusta yung weekend mo?
rounds.translation: Hey, good morning! How was your weekend?

chunks.note: Offices greet in English all the time.
Yung is the casual form of 'iyong', pointing to 'the' weekend.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Greet him and ask about his weekend.

rounds.situation: He asks how your week is looking.
rounds.tagalog: Grabe, ang dami kong deadlines this week.
rounds.translation: Wow, I have so many deadlines this week.

chunks.note: Start the thought with this reusable chunk.
Ang dami + ko + -ng: 'how many I have'. English nouns slot right in.
Time words often stay in English in Taglish.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Complain about your workload this week.

rounds.situation: You both glance at the calendar on his phone.
rounds.tagalog: May meeting pa tayo mamayang alas-dos, di ba?
rounds.translation: We still have a meeting at two later, right?

chunks.note: Pa means 'still, yet to come'.
Mamaya + -ng: 'later today, at'.
Di ba is the tag question 'right?' or 'isn't it?'

rounds.speakingPrompt: Double-check that you both have a meeting this afternoon.

responseExercise.promptTagalog: May meeting pa tayo mamayang alas-dos, di ba?
responseExercise.promptTranslation: We still have a meeting at two later, right?

options.englishTranslation: Okay, I'll just send you the file after lunch.
We still have a meeting at two later, right?
Come on, let's have lunch together later!

rounds.situation: Paolo needs a file from you before the meeting.
rounds.tagalog: Sige, i-send ko na lang sa'yo yung file after lunch.
rounds.translation: Okay, I'll just send you the file after lunch.

chunks.note: I- + English verb, with a hyphen, makes a Tagalog verb: i-send.
Sa'yo is the spoken short form of 'sa iyo'.
Use this ending to complete the spoken thought naturally.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Promise to send him the file after lunch.

rounds.situation: It's almost noon. Suggest eating together.
rounds.tagalog: Tara, sabay na tayong mag-lunch mamaya!
rounds.translation: Come on, let's have lunch together later!

chunks.note: Tara means 'let's go'.
Sabay means 'at the same time, together'. Tayo + -ng links to the verb.
Mag- + English noun: 'to have lunch'.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Invite him to eat lunch with you.

responseExercise.promptTranslation: Come on, let's have lunch together later!

lessons.summary: Dawn Mass, Noche Buena and greeting your godparents.

content.title: Christmas in the Philippines
content.scenario: Dawn Mass, Noche Buena and greeting your godparents.

rounds.situation: It's 3:30 in the morning in December. Your cousin is still half asleep on the sofa.
rounds.tagalog: Tara na, alas-kuwatro magsisimula ang Simbang Gabi.
rounds.translation: Come on, Simbang Gabi starts at four.

chunks.note: Na adds urgency: 'let's go now'.
Magsisimula is the future of magsimula.
The dawn Masses held for nine days before Christmas.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Hurry your cousin along to the dawn Mass.

rounds.situation: Mass is ending. You can already smell the food stalls outside the church.
rounds.tagalog: Bili tayo ng bibingka at puto bumbong paglabas natin.
rounds.translation: Let's buy bibingka and puto bumbong when we get out.

chunks.note: Bare root + tayo is a casual 'let's': bili tayo.
Two Christmas rice cakes.
Pag- + verb root means 'when, upon'.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Suggest getting the classic rice cakes after Mass.

rounds.situation: Christmas Eve. The clock strikes midnight and the table is full.
rounds.tagalog: Alas-dose na! Tara, mag-Noche Buena na tayo.
rounds.translation: It's midnight! Come on, let's have Noche Buena.

chunks.note: Start the thought with this reusable chunk.
Keep this chunk together in the middle of the sentence.
Mag- turns an event into a verb: 'to do Noche Buena'.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Announce it's midnight and call everyone to eat.

responseExercise.promptTagalog: Alas-dose na! Tara, mag-Noche Buena na tayo.
responseExercise.promptTranslation: It's midnight! Come on, let's have Noche Buena.

options.englishTranslation: Merry Christmas, Ninong! Your blessing, please.
It's midnight! Come on, let's have Noche Buena.
Oh, you didn't have to. Thank you, Ninang!

rounds.situation: On Christmas Day your godfather arrives. You take his hand and press it to your forehead.
rounds.tagalog: Maligayang Pasko po, Ninong! Mano po.
rounds.translation: Merry Christmas, Ninong! Your blessing, please.

chunks.note: Start the thought with this reusable chunk.
Ninong and ninang are your godparents.
Say it as you press an elder's hand to your forehead.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Greet your godfather and ask for his blessing.

rounds.situation: Your godmother hands you an envelope with a gift inside.
rounds.tagalog: Naku, nag-abala pa po kayo. Salamat po, Ninang!
rounds.translation: Oh, you didn't have to. Thank you, Ninang!

chunks.note: Start the thought with this reusable chunk.
The polite way to receive a gift: 'you shouldn't have'.
Use this ending to complete the spoken thought naturally.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Thank your godmother warmly for the gift.

lessons.summary: Sort out a mix-up politely but firmly.

content.title: Wrong order at the restaurant
content.scenario: Sort out a mix-up politely but firmly.

rounds.situation: The waiter puts a bowl of soup in front of you. It's not what you asked for.
rounds.tagalog: Excuse me po, hindi po ito yung in-order ko.
rounds.translation: Excuse me, this isn't what I ordered.

chunks.note: English 'excuse me' plus po is standard with staff.
Keep this chunk together in the middle of the sentence.
In- + English verb with a hyphen: 'in-order' means 'ordered'.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Get the waiter's attention and say it's the wrong dish.

rounds.situation: The waiter looks confused and checks his notepad.
rounds.tagalog: Sinigang na baboy po ang in-order ko, hindi sinigang na hipon.
rounds.translation: I ordered pork sinigang, not shrimp sinigang.

chunks.note: Na links the dish to its main ingredient.
Keep this chunk together in the middle of the sentence.
Use this ending to complete the spoken thought naturally.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Explain which dish you ordered and which one you got.

rounds.situation: Your friends have already finished eating. Make it clear this has taken too long.
rounds.tagalog: Kalahating oras na po kaming naghihintay.
rounds.translation: We've already been waiting for half an hour.

chunks.note: Kalahati + -ng: 'half an hour'.
Naghihintay is the ongoing form: the wait is still going on.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Say firmly how long you've been waiting.

responseExercise.promptTagalog: Kalahating oras na po kaming naghihintay.
responseExercise.promptTranslation: We've already been waiting for half an hour.

options.englishTranslation: Can you replace it right away? I'm allergic to shrimp.
We've already been waiting for half an hour.
Please just remove the shrimp from the bill. Thank you.

rounds.situation: The waiter offers to fix it. Shrimp is a real problem for you.
rounds.tagalog: Pwede po bang palitan ninyo agad? May allergy po ako sa hipon.
rounds.translation: Can you replace it right away? I'm allergic to shrimp.

chunks.note: Start the thought with this reusable chunk.
Agad means 'immediately'.
Keep this chunk together in the middle of the sentence.
Use this ending to complete the spoken thought naturally.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Ask for a quick replacement and explain your allergy.

rounds.situation: The right dish finally arrives. When the bill comes, the shrimp soup is still on it.
rounds.tagalog: Pakitanggal na lang po yung hipon sa bill. Salamat po.
rounds.translation: Please just remove the shrimp from the bill. Thank you.

chunks.note: Paki- + verb is a polite 'please': pakitanggal.
Keep this chunk together in the middle of the sentence.
Use this ending to complete the spoken thought naturally.

rounds.speakingPrompt: Ask firmly but politely for the wrong dish to be taken off the bill.
